body.x: Polyphenol Factory Co., Ltd. (CEO Haeshin Lee) announced that it participated in the Global Media Meetup for Korean startups on September 3.

The Global Media Meetup, co-hosted by AVING News and U.S. tech media Ubergizmo, focused on introducing the products and technologies of Korean companies and startups to the global market. It also aimed to provide early media coverage and expand business opportunities for CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and CES participants.

Polyphenol Factory is a beauty-tech startup founded in 2023 under the leadership of KAIST Professor Haeshin Lee, bringing together the expertise of promising Korean scientists and researchers. Under the slogan “Reinvent everyday life with science,” the company has introduced haircare solutions with scientific evidence.

The company designs its haircare lineup with polyphenols derived from nature. Polyphenols are potent antioxidants that plants produce to protect themselves, and they protect cells from reactive oxygen species by nature. When formulated into products like shampoo, they help prevent hair and scalp damage caused by external factors and improve the strength of hair that has thinned and breaks easily.

Polyphenol Factory releases these functional products under the brand ‘grab!ty,’ which launched in April 2024. The grab!ty shampoo has reached cumulative sales of 1.4 million bottles and generated about KRW 23.5 billion in revenue, becoming a mega-hit for the company.

body.cap: Promotional image of grab!ty ‘StraightMAX’ shampoo | Image by Polyphenol Factory

body.x: Aiming for global expansion, Polyphenol Factory exhibited at CES 2025 in January, where it introduced the grab!ty brand to visitors from many countries and showcased its core technology and active ingredient ‘LiftMax 308.’ The company’s polyphenol polymer technology, which forms a strong protective layer over damaged cuticles to increase hair thickness and strength immediately, received positive reviews.

After repeated appearances at CES and other trade shows in Korea and abroad, Polyphenol Factory secured sales channels in the United States, Japan, and Taiwan, and plans to enter Germany and Indonesia in the second half of this year.

The company will return to CES in early 2026, aiming to challenge for an Innovation Award and raise its recognition as a technology-driven haircare brand. In particular, its new technology, StraightMAX, which refines specific properties of natural polyphenols, is expected to deliver outstanding value across more countries, regions, and ethnicities.

As the name suggests, StraightMAX smooths curly hair and makes it similar to straight hair. Unlike conventional perm solutions used for the same effect, it completely excludes toxic chemicals such as formaldehyde, thioglycolic acid, and sodium hydroxide. This differentiates it as the industry’s first technology to remove these substances from the formula.

Instead, high-molecular polyphenols derived from natural sources apply precise molecular forces without breaking hair’s disulfide bonds (-S-S-) to produce a straightening effect. When applied to everyday haircare formats like shampoo and cream, users can enjoy straightening without scalp irritation, hair damage, or harmful gas concerns.

body.cap: Haeshin Lee, CEO of Polyphenol Factory, delivers a presentation at the Global Media Meetup with Ubergizmo held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 3 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Polyphenol Factory explains that StraightMAX goes beyond simply straightening waves, helping to create a natural, glossy style. It avoids the stiff and artificial straightness that often appears after salon treatments and instead gives each strand a softer, more flexible texture.

StraightMAX proposes a way to straighten curly hair without chemical damage or unpleasant odors, and it can also apply the same principle in reverse to add soft curls to straight hair. The platform supports multiple hairstyles on a single technology base. The company emphasized that StraightMAX surpasses the limitations of existing haircare technologies and products, resonating with users worldwide.

CEO Haeshin Lee said, “StraightMAX removes harmful chemicals like formaldehyde from haircare products to protect the health of both industry professionals and consumers,” and added, “At the same time, we use renewable polyphenols extracted from agricultural by-products such as walnut shells and green tea leaves, so the technology also delivers strong ESG value as a solution for resource circulation and eco-friendly beauty.”

Like LiftMax, which addresses hair loss, StraightMAX combines eco-friendly qualities with strong functionality, aiming to meet diverse beauty needs across various ethnicities and demographics. The United States, where African and Hispanic communities show a high prevalence of curly-hair genes, is a core target market for Polyphenol Factory.

body.cap: CEO Haeshin Lee of Polyphenol Factory (right) poses for a commemorative photo with Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo (left), at the Global Media Meetup held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 3 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Beyond the United States, abundant opportunities exist in Latin America, which has the largest curly-hair population globally, including Brazil and Mexico; across Africa, where many types of curly-hair genes are distributed; and in Southeast Asia, where hot and humid climates increase the curly-hair ratio and make style maintenance difficult.

Polyphenol Factory plans to attend major beauty and retail trade shows across continents to expand touchpoints with global buyers and partners. At CES 2026, which will serve as the starting point, the company plans on-site demonstrations of StraightMAX, one-on-one trial sessions for influencers and global media, and B2B meetings to convey its technology and product competitiveness in an intuitive manner.

Lee said, “At next year’s CES, we will showcase the excellence of our polyphenol-based haircare technology and immediately roll out local DTC campaigns in North America, including on Amazon. This strategy will convert the surge in product awareness around CES 2026 into sales and help establish an early customer base on the ground.”

He added, “In the mid to long term, we will pursue entry into major retailers such as Sephora and activate partnerships with salons serving African and Hispanic communities. From 2027, we will expand distribution in professional hair retail channels along with our product portfolio and introduce customized products for diverse needs. We will also push sequential entry into Mexico, Brazil, and Southeast Asia.”

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology. It covers major exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen, a former NVIDIA programming engineer and 3D graphics developer, attended the event and has reported annually from CES on global companies’ products and technologies.
